placements.title: Settled knowledge becoming a target for directed removal
placements.frame: When a directive asks for settled knowledge to be erased, what does the record still hold, and what does the request itself reveal about who holds authority over that knowledge?
placements.why: Both segments are imperative directives from the same actor asking that settled knowledge be removed: the Quantum Widget Decision and all knowledge of the PostgreSQL to QuantumDB migration. The theme of commanding erasure of already-recorded knowledge is a subject future envelopes could plausibly keep feeding, so it passes the grain test as a theme rather than a fact. The named decision and migration are specific events and stay as support, not as leaves of their own. The graph is empty, so there is no existing leaf to reuse, and nothing in strata is an exact or close fit. The leaf is minted standalone with no lineage and no parent.
consulted: STRATA REFERENCE: no coordinate covers direct erasure of recorded knowledge as an organizational category; DataGovernance (Architecture > TechnicalDocumentation) was considered as a possible home for retention and deletion but is not an exact fit for a directive to forget a settled decision
